### 1. Subscriber classes and what each may read and write

The class is chosen by the composition root at facet-issue time, not by the presenter. A presenter cannot subscribe as a class its facet was not issued for.

```gdscript
# Issued by the composition root in BOOTING, one per presentation object, never the whole Kernel (ADR-0001 § 5).
class_name PresentationFacet extends RefCounted
var views: PresentationViews          # ADR-0003 § 7; getter-only facades; perception access decided per facet
var clock: PresentationClock          # ADR-0001; read-only: tick_alpha, T, running, load_seq (§ 6)
func subscribe(handler: Callable, subscriber_name: StringName) -> SubscriptionHandle   # class fixed at issue; forwards to the kernel (ADR-0004)
# Content catalogs (ADR-0007) arrive as their own setup() arguments; they are frozen and read-only.
```

| Class | Facet is issued to | Reads | Writes | Submit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PRESENTATION` | Camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Failure & Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, the Filter's host object | `PresentationViews` of SIM blocks (previous and current pairs), `PresentationClock`, the frame's `PresentFrame`, frozen content catalogs, **products of strictly earlier stages** (§ 3), the Filter's `perceived()` for corruptible values | Only the allow-list below | Never. The facet has no submit method. |
| `INPUT_SURFACE` | Input Adapter (holds a `SurfaceHandle`), the Interaction prompt object (no handle), Chart Table menu objects (no handle at MVP) | As `PRESENTATION` | As `PRESENTATION` | **May be issued a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002); the class alone confers nothing.** Receives every tick's batch. |
| `PROJECTOR` | Layout projector (`body.projector`), Lighting's occluder builder | As `PRESENTATION` | Engine-side *derived* objects its block owner's GDD names (nodes it creates, frees or reparents; tile and occluder content); declares the engine classes it may instantiate at registration | Never |
| `DIAGNOSTIC` | Debug Overlay (dev and playtest builds only; ADR-0031) | Everything, including kernel internals and `PERCEPTION_OUT`, through a separate diagnostics facet | Its own overlay nodes only | Never |
| `REPLICATION` | Nobody at MVP (dormant until VS-B; ADR-0032) | n/a | n/a | n/a |

**Read rules, each lint- or boot-checked:**
- Presentation reads simulation state only through `PresentationViews` and `PresentationClock`. It never holds `SimViews`, a `WriteScope`, a `ctx` of a tick phase, or the kernel (a lint forbids those names in `src/presentation/`; ADR-0003 Risks already commits to it).
- **`PERCEPTION_OUT` blocks are not readable through a default `PresentationFacet`.** The composition root builds the Filter's facet (and the Debug Overlay's) with perception access; every other facet's `PresentationViews.get` on a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block returns that block's `empty_view` and counts `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`. Lighting reads the Filter's per-viewer decoy list, an object the Filter owns, not the block. This follows `architecture.md` § API Boundaries ("Filter and Debug only") and Principle 3 over the broader wording in the kernel GDD's CR-10 table; ADR-0024 defines the Filter's query surface and confirms.
- Presentation never reads another presenter's private state. A presenter may call a getter on a **strictly earlier stage's** product (the camera pose, the beam pose, the decoy list). Each presenter declares `reads: Array[int]` of stage ids at registration and the driver's freeze check fails boot if any entry is not strictly less than the presenter's own stage. A visual presenter never reads the Audio presenter or any audio level, bus meter, cue or voice state (TR-audio-042); Audio is stage 9 and nothing reads from it.
- The simulation (`src/kernel/`, `src/sim/`) never names a presentation class, a `Node`-derived class, `CanvasItem`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`. `zoom`, `k`, `k_auto` and `field_h` appear only under `src/presentation/` and the Pipeline root (TR-shipbody-044); a lint checks the identifiers.
- Presentation reads settings (reduced motion, reduce flashing) from the settings store; **no simulation callable reads a setting**, and no toggle writes a block. A test runs one command stream with each toggle on and off and compares the tick count and `state_hash` (TR-pxl-034).
- Cosmetic randomness: a presenter uses a stateless pure integer hash of its own keys (Filter PF-37), never the global RNG, never `RandomNumberGenerator`, never `rng_derive` for a cosmetic. A truth-channel visual that must match the simulation (a trail) reads `rng_derive` as the pure function it is and writes nothing back. The hash itself (32-bit masking, avalanche test) is defined with ADR-0005's hash family; see Open Questions.

**Write allow-list (PRESENTATION and INPUT_SURFACE):** `CanvasItem` properties (including `position`, `visible`, `modulate`, `z_index`, `frame`, `flip_h`, `texture` and so on, with the placement rule of § 4), `Material` and shader parameters, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties, particle properties, and audio-player and audio-bus properties through the Audio presenter. Never: a block, a command (outside § 7), a physics body, `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` members **outside the Pipeline root and the camera host** (PR-8 item 4 and its lint AC), `Engine.time_scale`, `SceneTree.paused` (pause is the control plane's `PauseGate`, ADR-0002), synthetic input (`Input.parse_input_event`, `Input.action_press`), and file I/O (Settings and the Save host have their own owners).

**The Layout PROJECTOR never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`** (TR-section-024); Lighting's occluder builder is also a PROJECTOR and is the one class that does. The declared-classes list at registration is what the lint compares. The PROJECTOR scene shape, the Y-sort key and `entity_id` namespaces belong to ADR-0034.

A presenter output signal that crosses into simulation does not exist: the flow is state, notification, presentation, and never the reverse (CR-10 "Sim never calls presentation").

### 2. Dirty-mark-then-draw

**The handler contract.** The kernel invokes each subscriber handler through a registered `Callable` with a reused `NotifyContext` (ADR-0003 § 3), exactly like every other kernel-invoked callable. The shape assumed from ADR-0003 and fixed by ADR-0004 is:

```gdscript
func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:
	_dirty.mark_from(batch)     # O(batch size), into a pre-sized structure; container type is ADR-0004's
	return ctx.complete()       # last statement; nothing follows it
```

This replaces the architecture document's `-> void` example (§ GDD sync). A handler **must** do only this: copy the batch's keys into the presenter's pre-sized dirty structure, copy the scalar fields it needs from an event record into a fixed-size ring, and return. A handler **must never**: read a view, touch a node, create a `Callable` or a container, emit an engine signal, `await` (ADR-0003's identity check turns a coroutine state into a recorded `INCOMPLETE`, which counts against the handler), call `submit`, or write any property. A handler fault is counted and never fatal (ADR-0003).

**Why the handler does not draw.** It runs inside P5 with writes disabled and its cost is added to every other subscriber's; a catch-up frame already runs the tick loop up to four times (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) and `INPUT_SURFACE` handlers run once per tick. Reading views there would also read a state that a later tick in the same frame is about to replace.

**Delivery recap (properties this ADR relies on; ADR-0004 owns the mechanism):**
- PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches arrive **once per rendered frame**, after the frame's last tick, with the union of `change_keys` (collapsing to `ALL` past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256). INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick's batch. A 0-tick frame delivers nothing.
- A restore delivers `ALL` for every block to every class once the kernel is `RUNNING` again.
- Notifications carry no state; event records (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`) carry identifiers only.

**The draw side.** Each presenter keeps two things, and its `present(frame)` early-outs only when both are empty:
- `dirty`: which blocks or keys changed since its last draw. Dirty drives **bulk and structural reads** (lists, queries, rebuilds, layout of plates): a presenter performs a bulk read of a block only when that block, or `ALL`, is dirty (TR-instr-005: derived inputs refresh once per Graph step because the Graph dirties its keys once per step, never per frame).
- `animating`: whether anything still moves on `tick_alpha` or `present_time` (an interpolated position, a needle ramp, a fade, flow scroll). **Interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification**, because a 144 fps frame between two ticks has a new `tick_alpha` and no new state; the example in `architecture.md` that returns when `_dirty.is_empty()` would freeze motion on those frames and is corrected. Cheap scalar getters on the `interpolated` pair (previous and current position) may be read every frame while `animating`.
- `ALL` means "rebuild everything from the views, and draw the end state with no transition": the correct and sufficient response both to a restore and to a mass change. A presenter bounds a rebuild by its own budget (PROJECTOR: `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`, chunked across frames, continuing to draw the last complete state until the chunks finish).
- Event records are copied into a fixed ring; ring overflow degrades to a full rebuild and counts `PRESENTER_EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are never dropped silently, and a `BODY_TRANSFER` is delivered to the camera as a rebase, not a cut (TR-shipbody-049; the rebase math is ADR-0008's).

**Coherence by construction.** The driver runs after the TickDriver in the same `_process` pass (priorities -50 then 0) and the kernel cannot tick while presentation runs, so every presenter in a frame reads the same committed tick `T`. No presenter copies state to be consistent.

**Latency, stated honestly.** Discrete committed state (a bead appears, a light toggles) is drawn in the same rendered frame as the P5 that announced it, with zero frames of delay (TR-assembly-045). Continuously interpolated motion lags the commit by up to one tick by construction, because `tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 and never extrapolates (PR-4 rule 3, PR-9 rate table).

**A debug-build safety net, in addition to ADR-0004's check that every changed block marked a dirty key:** every presenter exposes `rebuild_signature() -> int` in debug and test builds only (a hash of the presenter's derived draw model). The dirty-correctness test (Validation) runs a scripted command stream through an incrementally updated presenter and a fresh presenter fed `ALL`, and requires equal signatures. A presenter that forgot to react to a key is caught by that test, not in play.

### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages

**A single `PresentationHost` node** (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code) owns a `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls `driver.frame(...)` from its `_process`. The host is the Pipeline root or a node it owns (ADR-0008 decides which; either way exactly one node). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.

This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result that KRN-LAT-02 has not yet confirmed for a rendering build. Only the order **host after TickDriver** depends on ADR-0001's verified order.

```gdscript
# src/presentation/presentation_stage.gd. Named constants only; nobody writes a literal stage number.
class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted
const INTENT: int = 0          # UI INPUT_SURFACE objects submit latched intents (§ 7)
const PROJECT: int = 1         # PROJECTOR builds and rebuilds, chunked
const CAMERA_SOLVE: int = 2    # CameraSolver computes pose_q and world_to_hud; the canvas write is in frame_pre_draw
const AVATAR: int = 3          # Avatar Presenter: position, frame, flip, beam pose
const FILTER: int = 4          # Perception Filter step, decoy list, perceived() memo
const INSTRUMENTS: int = 5
const HUD: int = 6
const LIGHTING: int = 7        # reads the beam pose (AVATAR) and the decoy list (FILTER)
const TRAIL: int = 8           # Failure & Trail (truth channel, reads no Filter product)
const AUDIO: int = 9
const DEBUG: int = 10
```

**The pinned partial order and why this total order satisfies it.** Every source that states an edge is satisfied:
- HUD AC-HS-89 and TR-hud-022: camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting. Stages 2, 3, 4, 6, 7.
- PF-35 and TR-percfilter-025: Avatar, then Filter, then Lighting reads the decoy list. Stages 3, 4, 7.
- TR-pc-040: the Presenter's beam pose is written before Lighting applies. Stages 3, 7.
- Instruments call `perceived()`, so they follow the Filter. Stages 4, 5.
- The rest (Trail, Audio, Debug after Lighting) is a convention. It differs from the order in `architecture.md` § Data Flow (Avatar, Lighting, Trail, Instruments, HUD, Audio), which the three GDD-stated edges override; § GDD sync lists the rewrite.
- **Camera versus Avatar.** Pipeline C2 asks for the camera "ordered after the actor" so that both compose the same interpolated position. This ADR gets the same guarantee by construction, not by order: the solver and the Avatar Presenter both call `Placement.at` with the same `PresentFrame` values, so they cannot disagree. The solver runs first because the HUD needs `world_to_hud` before it draws (TR-hud-022). Step 12 of the pipeline spike (zero render-px disagreement) tests the claim.

```gdscript
class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
var name: StringName
var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void
var on_discontinuity: Callable        # (kind: int) -> void; DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE or DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT

class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
var alpha: float            # clock.tick_alpha read ONCE per frame; in [0, 1]; 1.0 while not RUNNING
var T: int                  # last committed tick; may feed values the simulation also computes, never cosmetic phase
var running: bool
var present_time: float     # supplied by the Pipeline root (ADR-0008); frozen while PAUSED; the only cosmetic clock
var render_delta: float     # for smoothing filters only; never a phase

class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted
func register(desc: PresenterDescriptor) -> void          # BOOTING only
func freeze() -> void                                      # sorts by stage; checks reads < stage; unique names; fails boot otherwise
func frame(host_delta: float, present_time: float) -> void # fills PresentFrame, handles load_seq, runs the stages
func notify_camera_cut() -> void                           # called by the camera stage; next frame every presenter gets CAMERA_CUT
```

`present` and `on_discontinuity` are registered `Callable`s returning `void`. They are **not** kernel-invoked owner callables, so ADR-0003's `CompletionToken` rule does not apply to them, and registering `Callable`s rather than overriding a base class avoids the 4.7 typed-return override rule altogether (ADR-0003 § 1 makes the same choice for owners). If ADR-0010 picks an `@abstract` base class instead, `-> void` overrides need no `return`.

**Driver rules.** The driver iterates a fixed-size array, allocates nothing, checks `present.is_valid()` before each call and skips and counts a freed presenter (`PRESENTER_DEAD`, as ADR-0002 does for result handlers), and **never runs a presenter inside a tick**. Presenter faults cannot fault the kernel: nothing here runs in a tick phase. Stage timing exists in dev and playtest builds through ADR-0001's diagnostics timer and is compiled out of release.

**The frame object is the clock.** `PresentFrame.alpha` is read once; no presenter reads `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` directly (a lint on `tick_alpha` outside the driver, the camera solver's pure-function twin and tests). This guarantees one alpha per frame. A presenter may read `frame.T` for values the simulation also computes (the beacon aim at `T`, a Graph step index); it **must never** use `T` or any tick counter as cosmetic phase (registry `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`), and uses `frame.present_time` for cosmetic phase.

**Pause.** `PresentFrame.present_time` is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and `alpha` is 1.0, so a presenter that computes from `present_time` and `alpha` is frozen without being told. Layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table) keep running on engine time because they must respond while paused (PR-9); they are INPUT_SURFACE objects and UI Controls, not world presenters.

### 4. Integer placement at `tick_alpha`

One function, one owner, no other rounding anywhere in presentation.

```gdscript
# src/presentation/placement.gd
class_name Placement extends RefCounted
## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
static func at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) -> Vector2i:
	return Vector2i(floori(prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha), floori(prev.y + (curr.y - prev.y) * alpha))

## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
	return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)

## The only assignment point for a Node2D position in presentation. Skips an unchanged write.
static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
	var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
	if node.position != v:
		node.position = v
```

**Rules:**
- Every moving thing in the current body frame is placed with `Placement.at` and written with `Placement.put`: sprites, the avatar, hand tools, the beam chest point, light origins, HUD plate anchors that follow world things, the single floored canvas offset of a non-avatar body (`Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, alpha)` with both offsets taken relative to the avatar's body, TR-shipbody-033), and the camera pose. The beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position, so light origin and sprite never disagree (PR-4 rule 2, TR-pc-026).
- **`floori`, never `int()`, `round`, `roundi` or truncation.** Probed 2026-10-28: `floori(-3 + 1 * 0.5)` is -3. Truncation and rounding both move negative-coordinate bodies by a pixel relative to positive ones.
- **Interpolate, then quantise (PR-4 rule 3).** Snap is a floor, not a filter: a body moving one base pixel per tick shows a k by k block step at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above, never backward. Nothing is rounded before the lerp.
- `alpha` is `frame.alpha`, in [0, 1], never extrapolated. `alpha_n` is legal only for a block whose owner publishes its run tick, is clamped at 1, and is floored by `at`. The sprite pose of a stepped rig (Horror) is not tweened; only the record's position is placed with `alpha_n` (PR-9).
- **Assignments to `position`, `global_position`, `transform`, `global_transform`, `offset` or `canvas_transform` on a `Node2D` or `CanvasItem` appear only in `placement.gd`** (and in the camera host's one `canvas_transform` write); a lint enforces it. A debug-build and integration-test sweep reads every `Node2D` under the world root once per frame in the scripted walk and asserts a zero fractional part (`PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` counts, test fails on non-zero).
- No per-node scale animation; horizontal flip is `flip_h` or a scale of -1 on x only; `Camera2D.zoom` stays (1, 1); rotation of human-built geometry is 0 (PR-4 rules 4 and 5). Cosmetic offsets (tremor of plus or minus 1 art px) are integers added after placement.
- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` are on as a safety net, set to their required values in `project.godot` by the Pipeline's guard rails (PR-15; probed: both default `false`). **Nothing in this ADR relies on them**; what they snap to under the SubViewport variants is ADR-0008's spike.
- An asset or one-off sprite uses even cell dimensions or `centered = false` with an integer `offset` (PR-4 rule 6); the asset lint is ADR-0010's.

### 5. One interpolator: physics interpolation off, and no engine clock on sim-visible content

**The pins.** `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false` in `project.godot`, written explicitly by the Pipeline's guard-rail block (PR-15; a value equal to the default is not serialised, so the tests read the effective value). The presentation root nodes set `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`; children inherit. `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false` and `limit_smoothed = false` where a `Camera2D` exists at all (the primary camera variant has none in the world tree, PR-6 C2).

**The boot check, after the first frame** (probed: inheritance resolves in a running tree and not before): `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/common/physics_interpolation") == false`, `get_tree().physics_interpolation == false`, and a walk over every node under the presentation roots asserts `not node.is_physics_interpolated()`. A violation fails boot in dev and playtest builds and counts `PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_ON` plus logs in release. A gdUnit4 test additionally turns `SceneTree.physics_interpolation` on, builds the presentation tree, and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node, which proves the `OFF` roots rather than only the project setting.

**Why not use the engine's 2D interpolation.** (a) It would be a second interpolator on a second clock (PR-4 rule 8). (b) Probed: `get_global_transform_interpolated` does not exist on `Node2D`, so no script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn, and the camera, which follows the un-interpolated pose, would swim against the sprite by 1 to 3 render pixels at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. (c) The kernel's previous and current pair is the only definition of the previous pose that survives a restore, a body transfer and a snap (`snap_baseline`, ADR-0003).

**Engine clocks on sim-visible content.** `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D.play()` and `GPUParticles2D` at a non-zero `speed_scale` run on the engine's process time, which does not stop under kernel `PAUSED` (the tree is not paused, ADR-0001 § 6) and does not follow reduced motion. For world content (layer 0) and the HUD (layer 2) a presenter therefore **drives animation from `frame.present_time`** (a frame index computed from it, a shader time parameter set from it) or sets `speed_scale` to 0 while `present_time` is frozen. Engine-clocked animation is permitted only on layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table and menus), which must respond under pause, and on content that has no sim-visible meaning and is allowed to continue. Whether `speed_scale = 0` freezes a given node type exactly is UNVERIFIED (PRES-SPIKE-1).

The bounded presentation-owned animation states are those PR-8 admits (camera state, and the instruments' `settle_response`), plus the cosmetic scalars of § 6.

### 6. Presentation-local state, the restore edge, and pure-function presenters

**What presentation may keep.** A presenter may hold a scalar or small structure (a needle's settle triple, a dwell counter, a tremor envelope, a fade, a cull history, the camera's smoothing state, a numeral throttle) **if and only if**:
1. it is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation (`src/kernel/` and `src/sim/` import nothing from `src/presentation/`);
2. it changes how a value *arrives* and never what it *settles to*, and never decides visibility of a truth-channel element (a trail's visibility depends only on the sim, which is why the Failure & Trail GDD calls it a pure reader);
3. it is reset by `on_discontinuity` on a restore, a new game, a camera cut and `hard_start` (TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047);
4. the presenter's registration lists it in a short doc comment so a reviewer can see the scalars (the lint cannot).

**A presenter's drawn output is a pure function** of `(PresentationViews at this frame, PresentFrame, its resettable scalars)`. The first frame after a restore needs no special path: `ALL` rebuilds from views, `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` clears the scalars, and the kernel's `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so there is no interpolation across the break (TR-cmd-046, TR-horror-041, TR-attention-047, TR-webmap-039 restore half). A multi-beat stall plays at most one beat and never replays (TR-attention-047): a presenter keeps the last-seen sequence value it was shown, compares it with the view's, and on a jump of more than one shows the end state.

**Edge detection by sequence counters.** A presenter detects a discrete source change by comparing a view's sequence counter to the value it last saw (`breath_src_change_seq`, TR-suit-041), not by counting notifications, because merged delivery turns N ticks into one batch. Because the notification, the dirty mark and the draw happen in one rendered frame, a click can start in the Audio stage and the dial swap land in the Instruments stage of the same frame.

**The restore edge is not `ALL`.** `ALL` also means "more than 256 keys changed this frame" (a weld can do it), and resetting an instrument's tremor on a weld is wrong. The driver therefore watches a dedicated counter:

```gdscript
# Requested of ADR-0001's PresentationClock (read-only, not a state block, never hashed or saved):
var load_seq: int:      # +1 on every transition into RUNNING that follows LOADING, and on every new game
	get: return _driver_load_seq
```

At the top of `frame(...)` the driver compares `clock.load_seq` with the last seen value and, on a change, calls every presenter's `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)` **before** any `present`. Camera cuts arrive the other way: the camera stage calls `driver.notify_camera_cut()` and the next frame delivers `DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT` (reset of instrument scalars and cull history; Instruments IW-33). `BODY_TRANSFER` is a rebase, not a cut, unless the new body's limits clamp (TR-shipbody-049, ADR-0008). If ADR-0001's owner declines the extra field, the equivalent is a restore marker in ADR-0004's `ChangeBatch`; the driver is the only consumer either way, so the choice does not leak into presenters.

### 7. `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only submitting class, and a class is not a right

- A command can be submitted only by an object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002) **and** was registered as `INPUT_SURFACE`. Subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` confers no submit right (registry `presentation_submit_without_handle`): the Interaction prompt object subscribes without a handle. A `PRESENTATION` facet has no submit method and no way to obtain a handle.
- **Boot check at the freeze:** every handle name in the kernel's issued-handle table corresponds to a subscription registered as `INPUT_SURFACE` with the same name; a handle issued to a name with no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails boot. This ties ADR-0002's table to this ADR's class (ADR-0004's `subscribe` carries the diagnostic name; Open Questions).
- **Where a submit call may occur.** The Input Adapter submits from its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER` (ADR-0001 § 3, ADR-0019). Any other `INPUT_SURFACE` object (Chart Table menus later, the Interaction prompt if it ever submits) **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits from its stage-0 `INTENT` presenter step in the driver. It never calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process` or a notification handler (ADR-0001 guideline restated). The cost is that a UI intent is queued after the tick loop of its frame and applied next frame, one frame later than the Adapter's, which is acceptable for menus and prompts. The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal.
- **Result handlers.** The kernel flushes the result buffer in the driver, before presentation; an `INPUT_SURFACE` result handler is a kernel-invoked callable and obeys the same contract as a subscriber handler: it records the result into a fixed ring and returns `ctx.complete()`. Display of a rejection happens in the object's `present` step.
- **The rule is per object, not per system** (CR-10): a HUD that grows a button splits into the HUD presenter (`PRESENTATION`) and a small `INPUT_SURFACE` intent object.
- Presentation predicts no outcome; the Adapter's pre-play of body motion and sound keyed by `correlation` is ADR-0019's, and light and effects change only on committed state (kernel anti-target: no client-side prediction at MVP).

### 8. Engine signals stay inside presentation

Engine signals (`signal`, `.connect(...)`) are used **between presentation objects for user-initiated events only** (a card opens, a setting changes, a button is pressed). They are never the kernel's notification transport (ADR-0004 decides that; this ADR does not pre-empt OQ-4), never carry simulation values into a simulation module, and are never declared or connected in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/` (a lint; the simulation is scene-tree free). A signal is not a way around the stage-read rule: a presenter that needs another presenter's per-frame product reads it through a declared `reads` edge, not through a connection.

### Key Interfaces

```gdscript
# ----- Issued by the composition root (ADR-0001 § 5); presentation objects receive only these -----
class_name PresentationFacet extends RefCounted        # see § 1
class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted        # ADR-0001: tick_alpha, T, running (+ load_seq, requested)

# ----- Handler (kernel-invoked; ADR-0003 callable contract; shape finalised by ADR-0004) -----
func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken

# ----- Driver (src/presentation/) -----
class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted        # constants, § 3
class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted      # § 3
class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted             # § 3
class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted       # register / freeze / frame / notify_camera_cut
class_name PresentationHost extends Node               # setup(driver); _process(delta) -> driver.frame(delta, present_time)

# ----- Placement (src/presentation/placement.gd) -----
class_name Placement extends RefCounted                # at / alpha_n / put, § 4

const DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE: int = 0
const DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT: int = 1
```

### Implementation Guidelines
- **Must** subscribe through a `PresentationFacet` the composition root issued; **must never** hold the kernel, `SimViews`, a `WriteScope` or a tick-phase `ctx` in `src/presentation/`.
- **Must** write a subscriber handler as "mark dirty, copy event scalars, `return ctx.complete()`"; **must never** read a view, touch a node, allocate, emit a signal, `await` or submit in a handler.
- **Must** keep `dirty` and `animating` separate; **must never** return early on an empty dirty set while a value is animating.
- **Must** perform bulk or structural reads only when the block (or `ALL`) is dirty; scalar getters on the interpolated pair may be read each frame while animating.
- **Must** register one `PresenterDescriptor` per system with a stage from `PresentationStage` and a truthful `reads` list; **must never** write a literal stage number, define `_process` in a presenter, or read a product of the same or a later stage.
- **Must** place every moving thing with `Placement.at` and `Placement.put`; **must never** use `int()`, `round`, `roundi`, a tween, an engine interpolation or any other rounding for a sim-owned position, and **must never** assign `position`, `global_position`, `transform` or `offset` outside `placement.gd`.
- **Must** read alpha only from `PresentFrame`; **must never** read `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` in a presenter, extrapolate past 1, or use `T` or a tick counter as cosmetic phase.
- **Must** animate sim-visible world and HUD content from `frame.present_time`; **must never** leave a free-running `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D` or particle clock on layer 0 or layer 2 content.
- **Must** keep `physics/common/physics_interpolation` false, put `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF` on the presentation roots, and pass the post-first-frame boot walk; **must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/presentation/` (ADR-0001).
- **Must** write only the allow-list of § 1; **must never** write `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` outside the Pipeline root and the camera host, and **must never** write a block, a command, a physics body, `SceneTree.paused`, `Engine.time_scale` or synthetic input.
- **Must** reset every presentation scalar in `on_discontinuity`; **must never** persist, hash, replicate or feed back a presentation scalar, or let one decide a truth-channel element's visibility.
- **Must** submit only from an object that is both an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration and a `SurfaceHandle` holder; **must never** call `submit` from a signal handler, `_gui_input`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object, and **must never** infer submit rights from the subscriber class.
- **Must** use signals only between presentation objects for user-initiated events; **must never** declare or connect an engine signal in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/`.
- **Should** drive the driver with an injected `PresentFrame` in tests (stub presenters, injected `present_time`, no scene); **should** record stage timing only in dev and playtest builds.

## Alternatives Considered

### Alternative 1: Each presenter runs in its own `_process` at a named sub-priority of `PRESENTATION`
- **Description**: Add constants (`PRESENTATION + n`) per presenter in a presentation-owned file; every presenter node reads the clock itself. This is the shape `architecture.md`'s example implies and it keeps ADR-0001's "presentation nodes at `PRESENTATION` or greater" rule literally.
- **Pros**: Idiomatic Godot; no new host node; each presenter is an ordinary node with its own `_process`; no driver to maintain.
- **Cons**: Presenter order is N-way cross-node `process_priority` order, which KRN-LAT-02 has verified only headless for the three-constant case and not on a release export; each presenter reads the clock separately (nothing guarantees they see one alpha); order is untestable without a scene; a forgotten priority silently lands at 0 and runs in tree order; the HUD GDD explicitly asks for an explicit driver.
- **Rejection Reason**: The order is the contract (six TR rows), and an explicit array makes it testable and independent of an unverified engine behaviour. The cost is one small driver class. The decision is reversible: the `PresentationStage` constants map directly onto `PRESENTATION + n` priorities if the driver is ever dropped.

### Alternative 2: Draw in a `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` handler on the Pipeline root (PR-8 item 3 as written)
- **Description**: One engine signal handler on the Pipeline root reads views and draws for every presenter just before the frame is drawn.
- **Pros**: Guarantees every presenter has run before the draw; one hook for the camera write and the presenters.
- **Cons**: `frame_pre_draw` never fired in the headless probe and its ordering against `_process` is UNVERIFIED (pipeline spike steps 11 and 12), so every presenter would inherit an unverified dependency; presenters would run in an engine signal callback that the headless unit tests cannot trigger; the kernel's tick order guarantee (driver before presentation) is stated for `_process`, not for this signal.
- **Rejection Reason**: The only work that must happen in the draw phase is the `canvas_transform` write, and it stays there (ADR-0008). Presenters run in `_process`, where the order is stated, testable and already the foundation of ADR-0001.

### Alternative 3: Handlers read views and update nodes directly (draw in the handler)
- **Description**: The P5 handler does the reading and the node writes.
- **Pros**: Least code; no dirty bookkeeping; the draw happens as soon as state is committed.
- **Cons**: Writes happen inside P5, where a long handler stalls every other subscriber; in a catch-up frame it would redraw for intermediate ticks nobody will see (PRESENTATION delivery is already merged for exactly this reason); it cannot interpolate on frames that have no tick; it would read views that the kernel's own contract says are only coherent after P4.
- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts CR-10 and PR-8 item 3, and cannot serve a 144 fps render over a 60 Hz tick.

### Alternative 4: Rely on the engine's snap flags (and `physics_interpolation`) instead of an explicit placement function
- **Description**: Leave positions as floats, turn on `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and the engine's 2D interpolation, and let the engine quantise.
- **Pros**: Almost no presentation code.
- **Cons**: Snapping happens on the engine's float transform after interpolation by the engine's clock (a second interpolator); the Pipeline GDD records that what the snap flags snap to under the SubViewport variants is not sourceable; rotated or parented nodes snap differently; the camera and the beam chest point would disagree with the sprite by a pixel; the result differs between 60 and 144 fps in ways no test can see.
- **Rejection Reason**: PR-4 rule 2 already calls the snap flags a safety net, not the mechanism. One pure function is the only form of this rule that a unit test can pin.

### Alternative 5: Presenters keep their own previous and current caches and interpolate locally
- **Description**: Each presenter remembers last frame's value and lerps toward the new one.
- **Pros**: No dependence on `interpolated` blocks exposing a pair.
- **Cons**: Two definitions of "previous" (the presenter's and the kernel's); breaks at a restore, a body transfer or a hitch; moves the one interpolator into N places (PR-4 rule 8); a presentation that owns visibility-deciding state is no longer a truth channel (PR-8 rationale).
- **Rejection Reason**: The kernel's previous and current pair with `snap_baseline` is the only definition that survives discontinuities.

### Alternative 6: Let `PRESENTATION` subscribers submit through a shared handle
- **Description**: Give the HUD and Chart Table a shared `SurfaceHandle` so UI can submit directly from its signal handlers.
- **Pros**: Simple for menus and prompts.
- **Cons**: Collapses the distinction ADR-0002 builds (a class is not a right); makes "presentation never writes the simulation" unenforceable; blocks co-op ingress from being added without changing owners.
- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts the registered `presentation_submit_without_handle` pattern and kernel H4.

## Consequences

### Positive
- One place, one loop and one frame object decide presenter order and the alpha every presenter sees; the order is a list a headless test can assert, which closes the HUD GDD's ADR candidate F and settles the three-way disagreement over order.
- A handler has a single permitted shape (mark, copy, `return ctx.complete()`), so P5 cost is bounded by batch size and cannot draw or fault the kernel.
- Interpolation is one pure function; the camera, the beam, the sprite and a docked body's canvas offset agree by construction, and a cadence test needs no renderer.
- A restore needs no special presenter path: `ALL` plus a reset hook plus the kernel's `snap_baseline`.
- "Which class may submit" is now two checks (facet and handle) rather than a convention, and boot fails if the handle table and the class registrations disagree.
- The Layout PROJECTOR class rules and the write allow-list are stated once, in a form a lint can check.

### Negative
- A new class (`PresentationDriver`), a registration step and a frozen registry for presenters. Dynamic presenters (one per instrument) are not registered individually: one registration per system iterates its own children.
- Presenters cannot use `_process`, so ordinary Godot idioms for animation (tweens, `AnimationPlayer`) are restricted on layer 0 and the HUD, which costs authoring convenience.
- UI `INPUT_SURFACE` objects submit one frame later than the Adapter.
- Two requests land on neighbouring ADRs (`PresentationClock.load_seq` on ADR-0001; the handler signature and a restore marker fallback on ADR-0004), and several lint rules depend on ADR-0010's tool.
- The stage order beyond the three GDD-stated edges is a convention, and a GDD or `architecture.md` that disagrees must be edited (§ GDD sync).

## Risks
- **R1: `frame_pre_draw` ordering fails the pipeline spike** (fires before `_process`, or not in a way the host can use). Mitigation: only the `canvas_transform` write depends on it, and PR-6 C2 already names the fallback (the Pipeline root's own `_process` at the lowest priority, which still precedes the draw). No presenter depends on it.
- **R2: Release-export `_process` order differs from the headless probe** (host not after the TickDriver). Mitigation: KRN-LAT-02 is a precondition of Accepting ADR-0001 and therefore of this ADR; the fallback is the sequential-parent design recorded in ADR-0001.
- **R3: `Placement.put`'s equality skip is wrong for a node whose transform is also set elsewhere.** Mitigation: the lint makes `placement.gd` the only assignment point, and the post-frame fractional sweep in tests catches a stray writer.
- **R4: A presenter forgets to react to a key** (the dirty set is correct but the presenter ignores it). Mitigation: the dirty-correctness equivalence test (`rebuild_signature`) and ADR-0004's debug check; the first catches presenter bugs, the second kernel-side marking bugs.
- **R5: 4.7 `CanvasItem` lines lose their antialiasing feather**, which makes any `draw_line` hairline thinner than the art assumed. Mitigation: out of this ADR's decision, but the write allow-list does not make `draw_*` a placement mechanism; instruments use pre-rendered needle frames (TR-instr-010); ADR-0028 and ADR-0030 own the line-drawing consequence.
- **R6: A freed presenter or a stale `Callable`** at teardown or scene change. Mitigation: `is_valid()` per call with `PRESENTER_DEAD`; the teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value, as ADR-0003 requires of owners.
- **R7: `speed_scale = 0` does not freeze a given particle or animation node.** Mitigation: UNVERIFIED and spike-bound (PRES-SPIKE-1); the fallback is to compute the frame index from `present_time` and not use the engine clock at all for that node.
- **R8: The stage list is wrong for a presenter nobody has designed yet** (Interaction prompt art, a future overlay). Mitigation: the stage list is a constants file; adding a stage renumbers nothing that anyone writes by hand (nobody writes a literal) and the `reads` check re-validates the graph at boot.
- **R9: The `load_seq` request is declined by ADR-0001's owner.** Mitigation: the fallback is a restore marker in `ChangeBatch` (ADR-0004); only the driver consumes it.

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: The driver is a loop over at most 11 registered presenters with a validity check and a `Callable.call` each; it allocates nothing (one reused `PresentFrame`, one pre-sorted array). Handler cost is O(batch) merge into a pre-sized structure; it never reads a view. `Placement.put` skips an unchanged write. This ADR claims **no new millisecond budget**: presenter costs are already budgeted in their own GDDs and sum in ADR-0008's single draw-call and frame-time table (pipeline `_process` at most 0.5 ms, light CPU at most 1.0 ms steady, total frame at most 14.9 ms desktop and 30.0 ms Deck, P99, release export). Driver overhead is measured in PRES-SPIKE-1 and reported against the pipeline row, not given a number here.
- **Memory**: A fixed number of small objects at boot (driver, host, frame, one descriptor per presenter, one dirty structure per presenter). No per-frame allocation; verified by a flat `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` over N frames plus `is_same` identity of the `PresentFrame` and the descriptor array (OBJECT_COUNT counts only Objects, not arrays, per ADR-0007's note).
- **Load Time**: Presenter registration and the freeze happen in `BOOTING` with the kernel's registries; negligible.
- **Network**: None. Presentation is local; co-op peers draw their own views (kernel CR-10 notifications are identical for HOST and MIRROR).

## Validation Criteria
- **Order test (AC-HS-89):** a driver built with stub presenters in every stage, a stub Filter whose slew advances in its step, and an injected `PresentFrame` runs the stages in the `PresentationStage` order; the HUD reads the post-step value. A registry with a `reads` edge that is not strictly earlier fails `freeze()`.
- **Dirty-correctness equivalence:** per presenter, a scripted command stream through an incrementally updated presenter and a fresh presenter fed `ALL` yield equal `rebuild_signature()`.
- **Restore equivalence:** save at tick T, restore into a fresh presenter set, and compare the drawn signature with the continuing run after `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)`; both are the end state with scalars reset (TR-attention-047, TR-horror-041).
- **Placement:** property test over positive and negative prev and curr and alpha in [0, 1]: result is between `floor(prev)` and `curr`, never moves backward as alpha rises, equals `curr` at alpha 1.0, and `Placement.at` agrees across the camera and Avatar call sites for the same `PresentFrame`. A scripted walk with a fractional-position sweep every frame reports zero `PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL`. A 144, 120, 60 and 40 fps injected-delta fixture checks "never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above" and "alternating +1 and +2 at 40 fps" (PR-4 rule 3).
- **Cadence (TR-pc-039 half):** one command stream at 30, 60, 120 and 144 fps of injected delta: simulation blocks and per-tick presenter samples are byte-identical; per-frame placements are not claimed identical.
- **No physics interpolation:** the boot walk after the first frame passes; a test sets `SceneTree.physics_interpolation = true` and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node under the presentation roots.
- **Zero allocation:** `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` flat over 10,000 injected frames with the full stub stage set, and `PresentFrame` / descriptor array identity (`is_same`) unchanged.
- **Handler contract:** a handler fixture that reads a view, touches a node or allocates fails a counting stub (`HANDLER_VIEW_READ`, `HANDLER_NODE_WRITE` in test builds); every handler's last statement is `return ctx.complete()` (CI check shared with ADR-0003).
- **Class and handle:** a boot with a handle name that has no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or one issued to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails; the Interaction prompt object subscribed as `INPUT_SURFACE` without a handle cannot submit.
- **Toggle isolation (TR-pxl-034):** the same command stream with each accessibility toggle on and off yields equal tick count and `state_hash`.
- **Lints (ADR-0010 decides the tool; each is regex, AST or a boot walk):** writes outside the allow-list; `_process` or `_physics_process` in a presenter; `tick_alpha` outside the driver; `position`/`transform` assignments outside `placement.gd`; `int(`, `round(` on a placement path; `signal` or `.connect(` in `src/kernel/` and `src/sim/`; `submit(` outside `INPUT_SURFACE` files; `Camera2D`/`Viewport` members outside the Pipeline root and camera host; `SimViews`/`WriteScope` in `src/presentation/`.
- **PRES-SPIKE-1 (release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, shared with KRN-LAT-02 and pipeline spike steps 11 and 12):** host `_process` runs after the TickDriver; `frame_pre_draw` fires after the host's `_process`; `speed_scale = 0` freezes `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D` and `GPUParticles2D` under kernel `PAUSED`; driver overhead with eleven stub presenters is reported against the pipeline row.

## Open Questions
- **OQ-A. Presentation order is a convention beyond three stated edges.** The order in `architecture.md` § Data Flow (Lighting before Instruments and HUD) and AC-HS-89 (HUD before Lighting) cannot both hold. This ADR follows the GDD acceptance criterion and the Filter's PF-35. If the technical-director prefers `architecture.md`'s order, only the constants file changes and the HUD AC must be edited.
- **OQ-B. Who publishes the beam pose the rim fringe reads (TR-percfilter-043)?** The AVATAR stage (TR-pc-040) is assumed. If Lighting republishes it, the fringe needs a stage after LIGHTING. Decide with ADR-0028.
- **OQ-C. Camera limits ownership.** TR-shipbody-032 says `body.projector` owns `Camera2D.limit_*`; Pipeline C2 says `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at engine defaults and the solver is the only clamp (and the primary variant has no `Camera2D` at all); TR-pxl-017 says the PROJECTOR sets limits "consumed by the solver alone". Reconciliation assumed: the PROJECTOR publishes a limits rectangle to the solver and never writes `Camera2D.limit_*`. ADR-0008 and ADR-0034 confirm, and BDY-33 needs a wording fix.
- **OQ-D. `PresentationClock.load_seq`** (§ 6) is a request to ADR-0001. If declined, ADR-0004 supplies a restore marker. One of the two must exist before this ADR is Accepted.
- **OQ-E. Which node hosts the driver** (Pipeline root or a node it owns) and where `present_time` is advanced relative to `frame(...)`: ADR-0008.
- **OQ-F. The cosmetic hash** (PF-37 requires a pure integer hash with explicit 32-bit masking and no dependence on GDScript integer overflow) belongs with ADR-0005's hash family; the Filter GDD calls it an ADR candidate ("a PRESENTATION-only stream"). This ADR only forbids the global RNG, `RandomNumberGenerator` and `rng_derive` for cosmetics.
- **OQ-G. TR-pc-039 wording.** "Presenter frame/position/light logs byte-identical across render cadences" cannot hold for per-frame placements, which vary with alpha by design. The Player Controller GDD should say "per-tick samples".
- **OQ-H. The `PERCEPTION_OUT` read rule.** The kernel GDD's CR-10 table lets `PRESENTATION` read `PERCEPTION_OUT` views; `architecture.md` and Principle 3 say Filter and Debug only. This ADR takes the narrower rule and needs two views from `PresentationViews` (default and perception-capable). ADR-0003 § 7 describes one `PresentationViews`; ADR-0024 owns the final split.
- **OQ-I. Whether a PROJECTOR build chunk may run longer than one frame's slice** during a weld (453 tiles at 256 per frame is 2 frames; the weld frame may exceed the P99 ceiling by at most one frame, TR-section-025). ADR-0034 and ADR-0008.

- **Where a submit call may occur.** The Input Adapter submits from its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER` (ADR-0001 § 3, ADR-0019). Any other `INPUT_SURFACE` object (Chart Table menus later, the Interaction prompt if it ever submits) **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits from its stage-0 `INTENT` presenter step in the driver. It never calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process` or a notification handler (ADR-0001 guideline restated). The cost is that a UI intent is queued after the tick loop of its frame and applied next frame, one frame later than the Adapter's, which is acceptable for menus and prompts. The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal.

input.summary: ADR-0009 fixes the presentation subscriber contract that eleven presentation GDDs each restate: kernel-invoked handlers only mark dirty and return ctx.complete(), one PresentationDriver runs every presenter once per rendered frame in a named stage order over a single PresentFrame, and every moving thing is placed by the one function Placement.at (floori of the lerp at tick_alpha) with physics_interpolation pinned off and a restore edge that resets presentation-local scalars. INPUT_SURFACE is the only class that can be issued submit rights, and even it needs a SurfaceHandle; the ADR is Proposed, covers all 41 ADR-0009 TR rows by ID (with the Y-sort, scene-shape and camera halves sorted to ADR-0034 and ADR-0008), and records engine probes run on 4.7.2 headless, with frame_pre_draw ordering left UNVERIFIED for the pipeline spike.

registry_candidates.name: draw_or_read_in_notification_handler
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: draw_or_read_in_notification_handler
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "A subscriber, result or control-outcome handler only marks dirty, copies event scalars into a pre-sized ring and ends in return ctx.complete(); it never reads a view, touches a node, allocates, emits a signal, awaits or submits."
    why: "Handlers run inside P5 with writes disabled and their cost is added to every other subscriber; views read there may be replaced by a later tick in the same frame; interpolation needs draws on frames with no notification."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: presentation_write_outside_allow_list
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: presentation_write_outside_allow_list
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "Presentation writes only CanvasItem, Material, Light2D, LightOccluder2D, CanvasModulate, particle and audio members; never a block, a command, a physics body, Camera2D, Viewport, SubViewport, SubViewportContainer or CanvasLayer members (Pipeline root and camera host excepted), SceneTree.paused, Engine.time_scale or synthetic input; simulation code never names a presentation or Node-derived class."
    why: "Presentation never writes the simulation (kernel H4); a corruptible display must be a transform of presentation nodes only."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: engine_signal_in_kernel_or_sim
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: engine_signal_in_kernel_or_sim
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed; the kernel notification transport itself is ADR-0004's decision (OQ-4)
    description: "No signal is declared or connected in src/kernel or src/sim; engine signals are used only between presentation objects for user-initiated events and never carry simulation values into a simulation module or replace a declared stage-read edge."
    why: "The simulation is scene-tree free and testable headless; signals are hidden synchronous dependencies that bypass the stage-read check."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: unrounded_or_foreign_placement
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: unrounded_or_foreign_placement
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "Position, global_position, transform and offset of a Node2D or CanvasItem are assigned only in placement.gd (and the camera host's single canvas_transform write); sim-owned positions are never rounded with int(), round or roundi and never animated by Tween or AnimationPlayer; presenters read alpha only from PresentFrame."
    why: "One floor function and one alpha per frame keep the camera, the beam chest point and the sprite on the same pixel at every render rate."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: presentation_state_fed_back_or_persisted
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: presentation_state_fed_back_or_persisted
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "A presentation-local scalar is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation, never decides visibility of a truth-channel element, never changes what a value settles to, and is reset by on_discontinuity on restore, new game, camera cut and hard_start."
    why: "Restore must need no special draw path and a truth channel must stay a pure reader of simulation state."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

gdd_sync.old: ## Spikes that gate ADRs (table)

decisions.point: Scope sort of the 41 TR rows citing ADR-0009
decisions.chosen: Decide the contract halves here; send Y-sort key, door sort, z-bands, fallback, scene shape, per-body root, draw bands to ADR-0034, camera solver/limits rect/parallax/rebase/zoom ladder to ADR-0008, Lighting/Audio/UI internals to ADR-0028/0029/0030, TR-boarding-026 to the art bible; split rows appear in both tables with each half named
decisions.reason: Architecture v2 moved scene shape and Y-sort to ADR-0034 and ADR-0008 owns the viewport stack; deciding them here would pre-empt siblings

decisions.chosen: (batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken, last statement return ctx.complete(); mark dirty, copy event scalars into a fixed ring, nothing else
decisions.reason: ADR-0003 and the registry make every kernel-invoked handler return the completion token; the architecture example's -> void conflicts and is listed for sync; the identity check also rejects an awaiting handler

decisions.chosen: Presenters draw in PresentationDriver.present() called from one PresentationHost _process at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION; frame_pre_draw reserved for the Pipeline root's canvas_transform write
decisions.reason: frame_pre_draw never fired in the headless probe and its order is unverified, while the driver-before-presentation _process order is the foundation of ADR-0001; resolves PR-8 item 3 vs architecture.md

decisions.point: Explicit driver vs per-presenter priority sub-constants
decisions.chosen: Explicit driver with registered PresenterDescriptor Callables, presenters define no _process (host, INPUT_SURFACE nodes at INPUT_ADAPTER and layer 3-4 UI are exempt)
decisions.reason: HUD GDD asks for an explicit driver (ADR candidate F); one alpha per frame; order testable headless without a scene; avoids dependence on unverified cross-node priority order; reversible to PRESENTATION+n constants

decisions.chosen: PROJECT, CAMERA_SOLVE, AVATAR, FILTER, INSTRUMENTS, HUD, LIGHTING, TRAIL, AUDIO, DEBUG, with a boot check that every declared reads edge points to a strictly earlier stage
decisions.reason: Satisfies the hard edges in AC-HS-89, PF-35 and TR-pc-040 (Avatar before Filter before HUD and Lighting; beam pose before Lighting); the rest is convention and overrides architecture.md's Data Flow order

decisions.chosen: Each presenter keeps dirty (drives bulk/structural reads) and animating (drives per-frame interpolation); early-out only when both are empty; ALL means rebuild from views and draw end state without transition
decisions.reason: The architecture example's early return on an empty dirty set would freeze interpolation on frames with no notification at 144 fps over a 60 Hz tick

decisions.chosen: Placement.at = per-axis floori(prev + (curr - prev) * alpha), Placement.put the only Node2D position assignment point (skips equal writes), alpha_n for divisor-N blocks clamped at 1, snap flags only a safety net
decisions.reason: PR-4 rules 2-3 and 8; probe showed floori is correct for negatives and exact at alpha 1.0; one function is the only form a unit test can pin

decisions.chosen: Project setting and SceneTree.physics_interpolation false, presentation roots OFF, boot walk of is_physics_interpolated() after the first frame plus a test that turns the tree flag on and asserts is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled() is false
decisions.reason: Re-probe showed mode inheritance resolves only in a running tree (stale in _initialize), and Node2D has no get_global_transform_interpolated so engine interpolation is unreadable and unusable

decisions.chosen: World (layer 0) and HUD animation driven from PresentFrame.present_time; Tween/AnimationPlayer/AnimatedSprite2D/particles with a free-running clock only on layers 3-4 or non-sim-visible content
decisions.reason: Engine animation clocks do not stop under kernel PAUSED or follow reduced motion; speed_scale = 0 freezing is UNVERIFIED and bound to PRES-SPIKE-1

decisions.chosen: Only the Filter and Debug facets read the block; every other presentation facet gets the empty view; Lighting reads the Filter's decoy list
decisions.reason: architecture.md API Boundaries and Principle 3 say Filter and Debug only; narrower than the kernel CR-10 table; flagged for ADR-0003/0024 confirmation

decisions.point: Presentation-local state and the restore edge
decisions.chosen: Allowed only if never persisted/hashed/replicated/fed back, never decides truth-channel visibility, reset by on_discontinuity; driver detects restore via a requested PresentationClock.load_seq (fallback: restore marker in ChangeBatch), not via ALL
decisions.reason: ALL also means more than 256 keys changed (a weld can do it) and must not reset instrument scalars; TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047, TR-horror-041

decisions.chosen: Facet is issued per class by the composition root; submit requires both an INPUT_SURFACE registration and a SurfaceHandle; boot check ties issued handle names to INPUT_SURFACE registrations; surfaces submit from their own _process at INPUT_ADAPTER with intents latched in UI callbacks, never from a signal handler
decisions.reason: Registry presentation_submit_without_handle and ADR-0002; ADR-0001 allows any registered INPUT_SURFACE node below TICK_DRIVER, so no second submit location or stage is needed

decisions.chosen: Allowed only between presentation objects for user-initiated events; never declared or connected in src/kernel or src/sim; not the kernel notification transport
decisions.reason: Architecture Data Flow 4 states it; the transport itself is ADR-0004's (OQ-4) so this ADR scopes the rule without pre-empting it

decisions.chosen: Camera solver runs first for world_to_hud; camera and Avatar agree by calling Placement.at on the same PresentFrame, not by process order
decisions.reason: Resolves TR-hud-022 (solver first) vs PR-6 C2 (camera after actor); step-12 zero render-px disagreement test remains the check

decisions.chosen: Assumed PROJECTOR publishes a limits rectangle to the solver and never writes Camera2D.limit_*; surfaced as OQ-C
decisions.reason: TR-shipbody-032 vs Pipeline C2 (limit_* stay default, solver is the only clamp) vs TR-pxl-017; ADR-0008 and ADR-0034 confirm

decisions.chosen: Claim only that output is a pure function of committed state, frame.alpha and present_time with an injectable frame; byte-identical holds for per-tick samples, not per-frame placements
decisions.reason: Per-frame placements vary with alpha by design; wording flagged for the Player Controller GDD

decisions.chosen: Stateless pure integer hash only; never global RNG, RandomNumberGenerator or rng_derive for cosmetics; hash definition left to ADR-0005's family
decisions.reason: Filter PF-37 and restore-exactness; avoids deciding ADR-0005 scope

decisions.chosen: Claim no new millisecond budget; driver overhead measured in PRES-SPIKE-1 and reported against ADR-0008's pipeline row
decisions.reason: Presenter costs already budgeted per GDD and summed in ADR-0008's single table; inventing a number would be unsourced

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: ChangeBatch exists with int dirty keys (KIND<<32)|id, collapse to ALL past MAX_DIRTY_KEYS 256, PRESENTATION/PROJECTOR/DIAGNOSTIC batches merged once per frame after the last tick, INPUT_SURFACE every tick, a restore delivers ALL for every block once RUNNING; event records (BODY_TRANSFER etc.) carry identifiers only

The subscriber handler is a kernel-invoked Callable with signature (batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken (from ADR-0003 NotifyContext and the owner_callable_contract registry entry)

REQUEST: this ADR binds the subscriber class at facet issue and exposes subscribe(handler, subscriber_name) on PresentationFacet, forwarding to the kernel's subscribe(cls, handler) with a diagnostic name; ADR-0004 must carry the name so the boot check can tie ADR-0002 handle names to INPUT_SURFACE registrations

Fallback for the restore edge: if ADR-0001 declines PresentationClock.load_seq, ADR-0004 supplies a restore marker in ChangeBatch that the PresentationDriver alone consumes; kernel notification transport (OQ-4) is decided there and is not pre-empted by the engine-signal rule here

PresentationClock (tick_alpha, T, running) and ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION = 0 exist as written; REQUEST: add read-only PresentationClock.load_seq incremented on each LOADING-to-RUNNING transition and each new game; the host after TickDriver order is confirmed by KRN-LAT-02 on a release export

PresentationViews exposes long-lived getter-only facades with previous/current pairs for interpolated blocks and snap_baseline equalises them; REQUEST: § 7 describes one PresentationViews for PERCEPTION_OUT, but this ADR needs a default view returning the empty_view (counting PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED) and a perception-capable view for the Filter and Debug facets (amendment to ADR-0003 or confirmation by ADR-0024)

issue_surface_handle names are unique and recorded in the kernel's issued-handle table readable at the freeze, so the boot check can compare them with INPUT_SURFACE registrations; ControlHandle calls may be made from UI signal handlers (CR-15)

Presentation uses no rng_derive for cosmetics and no global RNG; the pure integer hash with 32-bit masking required by Filter PF-37 is defined with ADR-0005's hash family; ADR-0006: the LOADING-to-RUNNING transition after a restore or new game is the edge that bumps load_seq

The Pipeline root (or a node it owns) is the single PresentationHost, supplies present_time (frozen while PAUSED), owns the frame_pre_draw canvas_transform write, the viewport/camera/CanvasLayer property ownership, the physics_interpolation and snap_2d_* project.godot pins, the camera-limits rectangle consumption, BODY_TRANSFER rebase math, and the single draw-call and frame-time table

Decides the mechanism of each lint listed in Validation Criteria (write allow-list, position assignments outside placement.gd, _process in registered presenters, tick_alpha outside the driver, signals in src/kernel and src/sim, submit sites) and whether PresenterDescriptor Callables stay duck-typed or become an @abstract contract; ADR-0010 also owns the OBJECT_COUNT plus is_same zero-allocation verification

Owns the PROJECTOR scene shape, Y-sort key, z-bands, entity_id namespaces, draw bands and the camera-limits publication mechanism; this ADR defines only the PROJECTOR class rights and its declared-class list
The Input Adapter is the INPUT_SURFACE at INPUT_ADAPTER that submits from its own _process; owns the input-trace replay harness and pre-play keyed by correlation
Defines the Filter's perceived() surface, the per-viewer decoy list Lighting reads, and confirms that only the Filter and Debug facets read PERCEPTION_OUT; the Filter sits at the FILTER stage

Lighting is the LIGHTING stage reading the AVATAR stage's beam pose and the FILTER stage's decoy list; owns its Light2D/LightOccluder2D write set, the apply order inside Lighting and the 4.7 line-drawing consequence; if Lighting republishes the beam pose the rim fringe needs a post-LIGHTING stage

Audio is the last world stage and no visual presenter reads Audio state; ADR-0030: HUD/Instruments/menus register as stages, chart table layers 3-4 run on engine time; ADR-0031: DIAGNOSTIC facet and Debug Overlay are dev and playtest builds only

open_questions: OQ-A: Presenter order beyond the three GDD-stated edges is a convention; architecture.md Data Flow (Lighting before Instruments and HUD) and HUD AC-HS-89 (HUD before Lighting) cannot both hold. The ADR follows AC-HS-89 and PF-35; the technical-director may prefer the other order (constants file change plus one AC edit).

OQ-B: Who publishes the beam pose the rim fringe reads (TR-percfilter-043 says Lighting publishes it, TR-pc-040 says the Avatar Presenter writes it)? Assumed the AVATAR stage; if Lighting republishes it a stage after LIGHTING is needed. Decide with ADR-0028.

OQ-C: Camera limits ownership conflict: TR-shipbody-032 (body.projector owns Camera2D.limit_*) vs Pipeline C2 (limit_* stay default, solver is the only clamp, primary variant has no Camera2D) vs TR-pxl-017 (PROJECTOR sets limits consumed by the solver alone). Reconciliation assumed: PROJECTOR publishes a rectangle to the solver and never writes Camera2D.limit_*; needs ADR-0008/0034 confirmation and a BDY-33 wording fix.
OQ-D: PresentationClock.load_seq is a request to ADR-0001; if declined, ADR-0004 must supply a restore marker. One of the two must exist before ADR-0009 can be Accepted.
OQ-E: Which node hosts the PresentationDriver (Pipeline root or a node it owns) and where present_time advances relative to frame(): ADR-0008.

OQ-F: The cosmetic pure integer hash (Filter PF-37, 32-bit masking, no reliance on GDScript overflow) belongs with ADR-0005's hash family; the Filter GDD calls it a PRESENTATION-only stream ADR candidate.
OQ-G: TR-pc-039 wording: Presenter frame/position/light logs cannot be byte-identical across render cadences for per-frame placements; the Player Controller GDD should say per-tick samples.

OQ-H: PERCEPTION_OUT read rule: kernel CR-10 table lets PRESENTATION read PERCEPTION_OUT views, architecture.md and Principle 3 say Filter and Debug only; the ADR takes the narrower rule and needs two PresentationViews variants (ADR-0003 section 7 describes one).

OQ-I: Whether a PROJECTOR rebuild during a weld (453 tiles at 256 per frame is 2 frames) may exceed one frame; TR-section-025 allows the weld frame at most one frame over the P99 ceiling. ADR-0034 and ADR-0008.

Engine claims UNVERIFIED and spike-bound (PRES-SPIKE-1, shared with KRN-LAT-02 and pipeline spike steps 11-12): process_priority order and host-after-TickDriver on a release export; RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw order against _process (signal exists, never fired headless); speed_scale = 0 freezing AnimationPlayer, AnimatedSprite2D and GPUParticles2D under kernel PAUSED; cost of assigning an unchanged Node2D.position; version that introduced 2D physics interpolation; what the snap_2d_* flags snap to under the SubViewport variants (ADR-0008).

GDD text to confirm before editing: modular-ship-assembly MSA-39 (read only via TR-assembly-030), ship-body BDY-33 and the player-controller AC for TR-pc-039 were not read in full; the gdd_sync entries for those three cite TR text and say so.

toolu_01KDRKsr1YErh3qXTN3yQNq5.summary: ADR-0009 fixes the presentation subscriber contract that eleven presentation GDDs each restate: kernel-invoked handlers only mark dirty and return ctx.complete(), one PresentationDriver runs every presenter once per rendered frame in a named stage order over a single PresentFrame, and every moving thing is placed by the one function Placement.at (floori of the lerp at tick_alpha) with physics_interpolation pinned off and a restore edge that resets presentation-local scalars. INPUT_SURFACE is the only class that can be issued submit rights, and even it needs a SurfaceHandle; the ADR is Proposed, covers all 41 ADR-0009 TR rows by ID (with the Y-sort, scene-shape and camera halves sorted to ADR-0034 and ADR-0008), and records engine probes run on 4.7.2 headless, with frame_pre_draw ordering left UNVERIFIED for the pipeline spike.

    description: "A subscriber, result or control-outcome handler only marks dirty, copies event scalars into a pre-sized ring and ends in return ctx.complete(); it never reads a view, touches a node, allocates, emits a signal, awaits or submits."
    why: "Handlers run inside P5 with writes disabled and their cost is added to every other subscriber; views read there may be replaced by a later tick in the same frame; interpolation needs draws on frames with no notification."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: presentation_write_outside_allow_list
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "Presentation writes only CanvasItem, Material, Light2D, LightOccluder2D, CanvasModulate, particle and audio members; never a block, a command, a physics body, Camera2D, Viewport, SubViewport, SubViewportContainer or CanvasLayer members (Pipeline root and camera host excepted), SceneTree.paused, Engine.time_scale or synthetic input; simulation code never names a presentation or Node-derived class."
    why: "Presentation never writes the simulation (kernel H4); a corruptible display must be a transform of presentation nodes only."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: engine_signal_in_kernel_or_sim
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: engine_signal_in_kernel_or_sim
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed; the kernel notification transport itself is ADR-0004's decision (OQ-4)
    description: "No signal is declared or connected in src/kernel or src/sim; engine signals are used only between presentation objects for user-initiated events and never carry simulation values into a simulation module or replace a declared stage-read edge."
    why: "The simulation is scene-tree free and testable headless; signals are hidden synchronous dependencies that bypass the stage-read check."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: unrounded_or_foreign_placement
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: unrounded_or_foreign_placement
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "Position, global_position, transform and offset of a Node2D or CanvasItem are assigned only in placement.gd (and the camera host's single canvas_transform write); sim-owned positions are never rounded with int(), round or roundi and never animated by Tween or AnimationPlayer; presenters read alpha only from PresentFrame."
    why: "One floor function and one alpha per frame keep the camera, the beam chest point and the sprite on the same pixel at every render rate."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: presentation_state_fed_back_or_persisted
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: presentation_state_fed_back_or_persisted
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "A presentation-local scalar is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation, never decides visibility of a truth-channel element, never changes what a value settles to, and is reset by on_discontinuity on restore, new game, camera cut and hard_start."
    why: "Restore must need no special draw path and a truth channel must stay a pure reader of simulation state."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28

gdd_sync.old: func _on_kernel_changes(batch: ChangeBatch) -> void:   # marks dirty only; no draw, no read of other blocks
gdd_sync.new: func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:   # marks dirty only; ends in return ctx.complete() (ADR-0003 callable contract, ADR-0009 § 2)

gdd_sync.old: _redraw(Kernel.tick_alpha)
gdd_sync.new: present(frame) called by the PresentationDriver once per frame; early-out only when both dirty and animating are empty; alpha is frame.alpha (ADR-0009 § 2, § 3)

gdd_sync.old: Avatar Presenter → Lighting → Trail → Instruments (perceived()) → HUD (perceived()) → Audio
gdd_sync.new: stages: Projector, Camera solve, Avatar Presenter, Filter, Instruments (perceived()), HUD (perceived()), Lighting, Trail, Audio, Debug (ADR-0009 § 3)

gdd_sync.old: the pipeline root's `frame_pre_draw` handler, C2 `[UNV]`
gdd_sync.new: the PresentationDriver's present step, run from the host's _process at PRESENTATION; only the canvas_transform write is in frame_pre_draw (ADR-0009 § 3)

gdd_sync.old: every presentation node `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`
gdd_sync.new: the presentation roots are physics_interpolation_mode OFF and children inherit; the post-first-frame boot walk and the tree-flag test are the checks (ADR-0009 § 5)

gdd_sync.old: with `Node.process_priority` ordering it after the actor
gdd_sync.new: with the camera and the Avatar Presenter both calling Placement.at on the same PresentFrame values, so they cannot disagree regardless of order (ADR-0009 § 3)

gdd_sync.old: Read `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views; write only CanvasItem / Material / Light2D / particle / audio nodes
gdd_sync.new: Read `SIM` views; read PERCEPTION_OUT only through the Filter's facet; write only CanvasItem / Material / Light2D / particle / audio nodes (ADR-0009 § 1; confirm with ADR-0024)

gdd_sync.new: closed by ADR-0009 § 3: PresentationDriver stage order PROJECT, CAMERA_SOLVE, AVATAR, FILTER, INSTRUMENTS, HUD, LIGHTING; AC-HS-89 becomes the driver order test

gdd_sync.old: all drawing happens in the render callback
gdd_sync.new: all drawing happens in the LIGHTING stage's present step of the PresentationDriver (ADR-0009 § 3)

gdd_sync.old: In the render callback the Filter runs **after** the Avatar Presenter
gdd_sync.new: In the PresentationDriver the FILTER stage runs after the AVATAR stage (ADR-0009 § 3)

gdd_sync.new: The PROJECTOR / Lighting / Trail rebuilds are dirty-marked at P5 and performed in the driver's stages; the Emitter's re-derivation is the simulation hook emitter.place, not a subscriber (ADR-0009 § 2)
